Questions for practice consultant:

  • How can we negotiate with the insurance companies for better reimbursement rates?
  • What are current and projected salary rates for nurses and receptionists in this area, experienced vs new to practice?
  • What about Key IPA (contact: Ray Copridge, the Key administrator, 919-215-1366, a friend of Steve Leary) or other collective groups to increase negotiating power with insurance companies and for buying vaccines and supplies? 1-8-09, per Steve Leary, Key is currently only operating in Wake County. Leary suggests that I callKkey to see if they'd agree to my joining the group.
  • Which insurance companies reimburse at best rates, cover most families in area, and are easiest to work with/what companies do you recommend I accept?
  • Do you recommend a billing service in first year or two of practice and do you have any specific recommendations?
  • When should we have applications completed and submitted for insurance companies? per Leary: insurance companies may not want application submitted till 60 to 45 days before openiong the practice
  • How to obtain applications for insurance companies: per Leary, look on NC medical Society webpage for a uniform application.
  • inspections of facility? What is needed after renovations? OSHA?
  • Vaccines, how to obtain; available from state for no charge, which ones? Are there buying coops in NC to decrease cost of those vaccines which must be purchased (Menactra, Prevnar, Gardasil)?
  • What is attrition rate for patients in area? How many patients can we expect per month for first 12 months? How to model the growth of the practice?

1-8-09 I met with Steve Leary , president of Professional Management Healthcare Consultants Inc, practicing only with MDs and dentists since 1951. organization has 3 staff in their 20s, 2 in 30s, 1 in 40s and 2 in their 50s, including Leary. He is not a CPA but is next level down in training and can work with IRS. Consultants include accounting and practice management.

Their group manages 300 practices in NC, only a few pediatric practices; one practice in Orange County but not pediatric. he asked basic questions re: location, office, attorney, PLLC or other. We were interrupted twice by secretary looking for someone and then asking if he knew the password for someone's computer. WE talked for 1.5 hours. Advised to start with picking out the EMR and customizing it prior to opening;; recommended Myxis twice and gave contact name there, who is a friend of his. Will Ritout. Allscripts and Myxis have merged recently. He advised then making webpage with downloadable forms so that patient can fill them out correctly prior to office visit; stressed the importance of entering all information i.e. insurance card number correctly or else the reimbursement claim will be sent back. quoted cost for website set up of approx 17 to 24K. He advised to find out demographics of Hillsborough area, %ile on Medicaid from NC government sites, Orange County Chamber of Commerce, or Human Health Services. Medicaid is state administrated, although some of the money for it comes from the feds.Advised to minimize %ile of pts with Medicaid since they are the worst payer; usually advises to take no more than 25% of any one insurance company, although BCBS is a major player in this area and may be as high as 36% of the practice coverers.. This increases BCBS negotiating power, though. he offers tax planning services for practice and for us as a family. Retirement planning. Salary surveys and benefit plans for employees in this are; fee surveys by zip code. gave a recommendation for Cameron Cox, in hillsborough who has company that does billing.

advised to consider marketing to the Duke community and possibly link to Duke on website for pt information.

This company has fee of $150/hr, but sounded like they instead like to contract with you for once monthly visit, $400/month, either Leary or some of the others, (Anthony?), to come out to practice, look at the numbers, reimbursement denial rate, EOBs; talk to staff, than meet with MD for 1 to 2 hours. This fee should increase as the practice becomes more profitable. Extra fees for doing taxes, payroll, state something. He said that he would help me negotiate but not to expect much the first few years since I'm in pediatrics and a solo. Plan to renegotiate the next year's contract with insurance based on the data collected from the first months of practice showing good documentation and compliance with standards?. He advised to keep overhead low, although didn't specify much of how to do that except by having only a nurse initially who can also check people in, if I'm only seeing 6 pts a day initially, and then hiring a receptionist later. He did not seem familiar with the Orange County or Hillsborough areas.

Impression: he didn't seem much interested in my practice, probably because it is a small pediatric practice and won't bring in much revenue, compared to the other guys, surgeons, etc. Got the impression that they wouldn't charge me as much the first couple of years since I wasn't making money but then would start charging more. I wonder if they charge more to the surgeons and others who make more money and therefore are more interested in them. He did not have some info off the top of hs head that I thought was important, i.e. reimbursement rates in area, any info re: Orange County or Hillsborough (obviously didn't prepare for our talk by looking up any local Orange County info), etc. Seemed like an older good ole boy type although wasn't southern about it.
